target_state: implemented staging handoff. The complete 31-instruction body was re-derived from the image bytes for this package and matches the committed Ghidra listing instruction for instruction. All four virtual dispatches, the four short-circuiting full-32-bit equality tests, the two low-byte-only return sites and the two receiver displacements are modelled, and the model test kills 26 of 27 injected defects. The fourth return value is NOT asserted to be zero: 0x00641451 and 0x00641456 both write AL only, so the machine leaves the callee's own high 24 bits in EAX, and the four false exits are fully determined residue words. The dispatched callee is NOT identified and the four literals are NOT resolved: the six tables that install this body disagree about slot 9, and nothing in the body names the constants.

implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX and nothing else. Zero ordinary stack arguments is machine-observed: the only PUSH in the body is 0x00641410 PUSH ESI, there is no ADD ESP, and both returns are the one-byte C3 with no immediate (0x00641455 and 0x00641459). It is corroborated from outside the body by the single call site in the image, 0x00ec3b9c, which is a bare `E8` relative call with no argument setup.
implementation.return_note: std::uint8_t is the width the machine produces, and the C-visible result is therefore one byte. Both return sites write AL only: 0x00641451 is `MOV AL,BYTE PTR [ESI+0x26]` (bytes 8a 46 26) and 0x00641456 is `XOR AL,AL` (bytes 32 c0, not 33 c0); neither touches the upper 24 bits of EAX. The word the machine leaves in EAX is NOT a 0-or-1 word and is NOT a zero-extended byte: the upper 24 bits are the residue of the last callee's return word. The four false exits are FULLY DETERMINED, because each is reached from a CMP that has just proved EAX equal to a literal: 0xbcd73e00 from 0x0064141f, 0xb8669e00 from 0x0064142f, 0x37148100 from 0x0064143f and 0x04f68400 from 0x0064144f. The true exit is (callee4_return & 0xffffff00) | byte at receiver+0x26. The only caller found in the image consumes AL alone -- 0x00ec3ba1 is `TEST AL,AL` (bytes 84 c0) -- so the high bits are a register artefact of the original code generation and not a source-level fact. They are therefore NOT in the signature: the signature carries the one byte the body produces, and the residue is reproduced and asserted through the model-instrumentation word model_returned_eax() (changed by worker rp01, 2026-09-28; the declared type was `Word`/uint32_t before, which the listing does not support). Both readings are still asserted and both are still reported, and a per-run check pins the returned byte to the low byte of that word. A second, independent oracle agrees on the width: evidence_returns.classify returns WIDTH_1_IN_EAX, provable, over the complete 31-instruction listing.
implementation.receiver_model: an OPAQUE BYTE RUN with no member named at all: `std::array<std::uint8_t, kReceiverSize> opaque_00`, kReceiverSize 0x28. Nothing is named because the machine receiver record is `bounds_only: true` with offsets [0, 0x26] on ECX, which settles displacements but not member identities. The body reads the leading word FOUR times (0x00641413/21/31/41) and one byte at +0x26 once (0x00641451), and stores nothing; every access is a displacement through word_at / byte_at, and each displacement is a named constexpr pinned by a static_assert to the instruction it came from. The +0x25 byte that the neighbouring accessor 0x00641460 reads and the +0x28 word that the candidate slot-9 implementation 0x00641770 reads are properties of OTHER bodies and are deliberately absent -- given neither a name nor a constant. (Changed by worker rp01, 2026-09-28; the struct previously named field_00, field_04_25, field_26 and field_27, and Vtable previously named `slots`.)
implementation.dispatch_model: four indirect calls and nothing else. The receiver's leading word is loaded as a raw pointer word and then INDEXED THROUGH -- a two-level dereference -- and slot 9 (byte displacement 0x24) is read out of THAT, four separate times, each re-reading the dispatch word so a callee can change where the next call goes. The two dereferences are the header's word_at + dispatch_target_at pair, so the shape is stated once and cannot quietly become one level. The first call takes ECX as it stands at entry (0x00641411 MOV ESI,ECX does not change ECX and nothing before 0x00641418 writes it); the next three are preceded by MOV ECX,ESI because a callee may destroy ECX.
implementation.dependency_note: there are no direct callees to declare. The package header declares the slot type (Word (__thiscall*)(AssetData*)) and the model test defines eleven C++ observers plus one hand-written assembly trampoline that occupy slot 9 and the decoy slots.

mechanics.body_shape: alias the receiver into ESI; then four times in a row: read the receiver's dispatch word, read slot 9 (byte +0x24) out of the table it points at, and call it. After each of the first four calls compare the callee's full 32-bit EAX against a distinct literal and, on equality, leave through one shared false block that clears AL. If none matches, read one byte from the receiver at +0x26 and leave through the true path. Four indirect calls, no direct call, no store, no global.

frame_resolution.method: the body has no frame to resolve: no argument is pushed, no ADD ESP appears, and both returns are the one-byte C3, so ESP is at entry-4 (the saved ESI) at both return sites and back to entry at each RET.
frame_resolution.corroboration: the machine-derived ABI record independently reports stack_cleanup_bytes 0, side 'caller', saved_registers [ESI], ret_form RET; and the single call site at 0x00ec3b9c pushes nothing.

slots.entry-4: the saved ESI, parked by 0x00641410 PUSH ESI and given back by the POP at 0x00641454 (true path) or 0x00641458 (false path). Not a parameter and not a return value: both returns are C3, and the restored value is the caller's ESI by construction.

receiver_displacement.0x00: read FOUR times, at 0x00641413, 0x00641421, 0x00641431 and 0x00641441. It is the DISPATCH WORD: each load is of the receiver's own leading word (ESI = ECX, and there is no LEA, ADD or displacement on ESI anywhere in the 31 instructions), and its value is immediately indexed at the very next instruction.
receiver_displacement.0x26: read once, at 0x00641451, as a BYTE (0x8a 0x46 0x26). It is the body's only result-producing data. Nothing at +0x24, +0x25 or +0x27 is touched.

mechanics.receiver_writes: none. The 31 instructions contain no store to memory, so the model writes nothing on the receiver and the model test asserts a byte-for-byte match of the receiver block (past its leading word) and of both tables around every run.
mechanics.dereference_depth: two, on all four dispatches. `MOV EAX,[ESI]` loads a POINTER and `MOV EDX,[EAX + 0x24]` then indexes through it. A one-level reading of the same bytes would be `MOV EDX,[ESI + 0x24]`, which is not an instruction in this body.
mechanics.dispatch_word_reread: real and load-bearing. The four `MOV EAX,[ESI]` are four independent loads with a CALL between each pair and nothing else, so dispatch N+1 is decided by the value the word holds after callee N returned. The model performs four separate loads rather than caching one pointer, and the model test kills a caching model twice: once by having dispatch 1's callee overwrite the word (expected order A,B,B,B) and once by having dispatch 2's callee overwrite it (expected order A,A,B,B), which a model that re-reads only once cannot reproduce.

dispatch.slot_evidence: 0x00641415, 0x00641423, 0x00641433 and 0x00641443, all `MOV EDX,DWORD PTR [EAX + 0x24]`. The machine-derived dispatch record is silent on the slot (call_offsets [], vtable_shaped_loads 0) and contributes only the count of four.

mechanics.vtable_note: the slot index of this body and the CONTENTS of slot 9 were both read out of the tables' own bytes with GhidraMCP /read_memory, not inferred. 0x013ff648 is preceded by the dword 0x00000034 at 0x013ff644, the MSVC vftable header word, so slot 0 of that table is taken to be 0x013ff648 -- the same convention the sibling package pkg-swarm-w1-00641780 uses for the same table. The six tables disagree about slot 9, which is why no callee is named anywhere in this package.

short_circuit.shape: a four-way OR, evaluated in order, with one shared false target
short_circuit.observable_call_counts: 1, 2, 3 or 4 depending on which literal matched first; the model test asserts the count on every path, and the trampoline confirms the count of one at the register level on a false path
short_circuit.compare_kind: full 32-bit equality. CMP sets ZF exactly on bitwise equality, so signedness is irrelevant; two of the four literals have the sign bit set and still match. Not a null test, not `== 1`, not a magnitude or `< 0` test.

return_sites.0x00641451: `8A 46 26` MOV AL,BYTE PTR [ESI+0x26] -- an EIGHT-bit write into EAX. EAX still holds callee 4's return word (nothing writes EAX between 0x00641448 and here), so the word left behind is that return with its low byte replaced.
return_sites.0x00641456: `32 C0` XOR AL,AL -- also EIGHT bits, and specifically NOT `33 C0` XOR EAX,EAX. The upper 24 bits of the last callee's return survive.
return_sites.why_determined: each exit is reached from a CMP that has just proved EAX equal to the literal, so the residue is that literal with its low byte cleared. These four words are fixed by the instructions alone and need no chosen callee result to predict.
return_sites.caller_evidence: 0x00ec3ba1 `84 C0` TEST AL,AL -- the sole known caller reads the low byte only, so the high 24 bits are dead in practice.

semantics.claim: re_00641410(receiver) calls the receiver's slot-9 virtual up to four times in a row, re-reading the receiver's dispatch word before each call so that a callee may redirect the next one; if the FIRST call returns 0xbcd73e89, the second 0xb8669ec9, the third 0x37148141 or the fourth 0x04f684a4 it stops there and produces 0 in the low byte of its result; otherwise it produces the receiver's byte at +0x26. unresolved_questions: Which concrete function is reached at table slot 9? This body names no callee, so the answer is a property of the dispatch word the object carries at run time, and it is additionally unsettled by construction: the six tables that install 0x00641410 name four DIFFERENT functions in slot 9 (0x00641770, 0x00e31100, 0x00641850, 0x00b1e4d0, 0x00dd0e10, 0x00641770), so no single answer can be right for all six. A trace that records the loaded slot-9 address at 0x00641415 and the receiver's class at that moment would settle it.

What do the four literals 0xbcd73e89 / 0xb8669ec9 / 0x37148141 / 0x04f684a4 name? They are compared for full 32-bit equality against the value slot 9 returns, and nothing in this body -- no string, no import, no call -- resolves them. The nearest context is the adjacent predicate at 0x00ec3b60, which makes the same slot-9 dispatch and compares against a fifth literal 0x24720859; and in one table slot 9 is 0x00641770, whose whole body is `MOV EAX,[ECX+0x28]; RET`, i.e. a 32-bit identity word taken from the receiver. That suggests an identity or type tag, but it is a property of one table and one callee, and is recorded as context rather than as the answer. A vtable-detector pass plus the Sporepedia type tables, or a trace of a live object, would settle it; none was available to this worker.

What is the class of the receiver and what are its other members? Only +0x00 and +0x26 are reachable from this body. Two neighbouring facts are recorded and deliberately NOT modelled as members: the accessor at 0x00641460 reads the byte at +0x25, and 0x00641770 (one candidate slot-9 implementation) reads the dword at +0x28. The +0x28 sub-object is read off a CALLEE's body, not this one.

Does any real callee in this image ever change the receiver's dispatch word? The four independent `MOV EAX,[ESI]` prove the model must re-read it; whether the re-read ever matters at run time needs a trace. The model test proves only that the model is written to re-read it, which is a synthetic refutation.

Is the intended source-level return a bool, or the raw byte at +0x26? The machine forwards the byte unchanged, so a booleanised source is possible and a raw-byte source is possible. The one caller found (0x00ec3ba1) tests AL, which is consistent with either. Settling it needs a second call site or the original source conventions; this package asserts the machine behaviour and reports the ambiguity rather than choosing.

Does Ghidra have an SDK name for this member? It is FUN_00641410, it carries no namespace, and the live SDK-derived cSPAssetDataOTDB set that sibling packages enumerate does not reach this VA. A name from the ModAPI headers or a vtable-detector pass would settle it; neither was available to this worker.

Is the canonical return-type token a C type or a register-class label? The machine-derived record's own vocabulary for this target is 'integral_in_EAX' (reconstruction/evidence/00641410: both the abi and abi_derived layers carry abi.return_semantics = 'integral_in_EAX', and the nested `return` sub-record carries register EAX, register_class 'integral', type null). That token is a REGISTER-CLASS CLASSIFICATION -- it says the value travels in EAX and is integral -- and it is NOT a C or C++ type name, so it can never string-agree with a C++ declaration and is not a width. It is recorded verbatim in observed_original_abi.machine_return_semantics rather than in return_type, and the one-byte width is stated separately in machine_return_width, so the classification is kept without being adopted. What is settled by this package is the WIDTH (one byte, proven over the complete listing) and the C TYPE's agreement with the canonical claim; what is still not settled is whether the ORIGINAL source declared `unsigned char` or `bool` -- see the next-but-one entry -- which no machine evidence here can distinguish because the machine only forwards the byte.
